comment: The sole error was C versus D: D’s deeper SiLU network with two later LNs beat C’s shallower network with three early LNs. A plausible explanation is that early normalization changes input-dependent feature geometry, whereas later normalization rescales already transformed features; this mechanism remains unmeasured. K1039 helped place the rectifiers first, but cannot order two SiLU candidates. K1006 correctly warned against counting LNs; my prediction nevertheless favored C’s normalization/depth bundle without sufficient evidence. Backtesting a fewer-LN preference on shared-rate/momentum, equal-width, plain smooth univariate SGD history yielded only 1/7 wins across five questions. The lab contained no eligible comparable pairs. Thus this inversion supports a local placement/topology effect, not a validated general rule.

def target(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:

def synthesize(
